name: augustus
desc: Predict genes in eukaryotic genomic sequences
why: Real eukaryotic gene prediction you can run at home on a genome, a genuine bioinformatics rabbit hole.

brief.what_it_is: AUGUSTUS is a program that predicts genes and their structures (exons, introns, and alternative transcripts) in eukaryotic genomic sequences. It takes a genome sequence and can optionally take extrinsic evidence such as EST or mRNA alignments, protein alignments, and RNA-Seq reads, and it reports predicted gene models. It ships with species-specific parameter sets for many animals, plants, fungi, and some protists and bacteria, and includes a training program and optimization script so you can retrain it for a new species. It can be run on the web server, on a larger-input web service, or locally from source or packages.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a gene predictor for eukaryotic genomes that can be run locally, with an open-source build so users can compile it for their own platform. The README describes it as a program 'to find genes and their structures in one or more genomes.'
brief.how_it_works: The README gives little internal detail. The homepage says AUGUSTUS can be used ab initio and also has a flexible mechanism for folding in extrinsic information such as EST and protein alignments, and that it can report alternative genes with probabilities for transcripts, exons, and introns. Its training program estimates parameters from a set of known genes, and an optimization script tunes meta parameters such as splice window sizes.

brief.install_notes: Easiest route is the Debian/Ubuntu package (apt install augustus augustus-data augustus-doc). Otherwise clone the GitHub repo and run make augustus, then make auxprogs for utilities. You can install into a user directory and add bin and scripts to PATH, or install globally with sudo make install. Docker and Singularity build recipes are included. Windows users are pointed to WSL and the Linux instructions. If the config directory cannot be found, set AUGUSTUS_CONFIG_PATH, which the programs check first, falling back to ../config relative to the executable. Ubuntu 21.04 and Debian 11 onward support comparative gene prediction; older packages were single-genome only. The web server needs no install, and the homepage notes that the MediGRID option requires a registration by email for first-time users.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, widely used ab initio gene finder with a retrainable model and a flexible way to add evidence from cDNA, EST, RNA-Seq, and protein alignments, which lets it predict UTRs and alternative transcripts. The homepage says it is often the most accurate ab initio program for species it has been trained on.
brief.status: Unknown for last release or commit date; the README gives no date. Signs of active upkeep: source hosted on GitHub with a 'Build and test' CI badge, an issue tracker the README asks users to use, and current packaging in Debian and Ubuntu. The homepage's news items are dated 2009 and 2012, so that page is older than the code.
brief.caveats: Source is under the Artistic License (the README says so for src, scripts, and auxprogs). The README does not name a license for the data sets. Building from source is needed for the auxiliary programs, and the Ubuntu/Debian package covered only single-genome use until recently. Windows requires WSL. UTR prediction is trained only for a listed set of species (e.g., human, C. elegans, maize, honeybee, tomato). The web server is meant for smaller inputs; larger files need the separate web service or a local install. The homepage's species list is a training-set list, not a list of everything it can handle.
quotes: AUGUSTUS is a program to find genes and their structures in one or more genomes.
It is open source so you can compile it for your computing platform.
AUGUSTUS is retrainable. It comes with a training program that estimates the parameters given a training set of known genes.
